description: Adds sources to a report as datasheets, and answers their ids in the order of the sources. A source is a CSV file uploaded with createDataset, or a dashboard of a Looker, Metabase, Omni, Lightdash, Sigma, Tableau or Power BI connection: find it with searchDashboards, confirm it with the user, optionally check its tabs and charts with getDashboard, and add it by its connection, id and tabId from getDashboard's tabs, or from searchDashboards for a Sigma workbook found by a link (else the tab it opens on, a Power BI report's or Sigma workbook's first page). A dashboard comes in as one picture of the tab, read with the user's access to the connection, from which the slides agent can add its charts; a Tableau or Power BI dashboard's charts are listed when its picture is first taken. A source can also be a tabular or summary report of a Salesforce connection, found with searchDashboards and added by its connection and reportId: it comes in as a table of its rows, read with the user's access to the connection; a matrix or joined report is rejected. A source can also be a table or view of a Snowflake or Databricks connection, found with searchTables and added by its connection, database, schema and table: it stays in the warehouse, where the slides agent queries it with SQL with the user's access to the connection, as its default user when one is set, and the queries the agent saves run again on every update. A source can also be a range of a Google Sheets or Excel file the user added in the app: find the file with searchSpreadsheets, take the sheet's id from getSpreadsheet, and pass the range inside the sheet in A1 notation, like A1:F20. A range comes in as a table, read with the user's own Google or Microsoft account on every run. Pass the ids as datasheetIds on sendReportMessage for the slides agent to build slides from them. Only the report's editors may.

body.description: What the tool creates, changes or sends

sources.description: The data to add to the report, each source becoming one of its datasheets: an uploaded CSV file (`datasetId`), a dashboard tab (`connectionType`, `connectionId`, `dashboardId` and optionally `tabId`), a Salesforce report (`connectionType`, `connectionId` and `reportId`), a Snowflake or Databricks table (`connectionType`, `connectionId`, `database`, `schema` and `table`), a Looker explore, Power BI semantic model or Tableau data source (`connectionType`, `connectionId` and `modelId`), or a range of a spreadsheet (`spreadsheetId`, `sheetId` and `range`). An uploaded file, a Salesforce report or a range comes in as a table, a warehouse table stays in the warehouse and a model in its BI tool for the slides agent to query, and a dashboard tab comes in as a picture of the tab. If any source can't be added, none is. From 1 to 100 sources.

datasetId.description: The uploaded CSV file to add: the `id` returned by `createDataset`. The datasheet contains the whole CSV as one table and is named after the file. It can be any uploaded CSV file of the report's organization, including one another member uploaded; an uploaded workbook is rejected.

connectionId.description: The connection the dashboard is on: the `id` of a connection from `listConnections`. You must have access to the connection in Rollstack.

connectionType.description: The type of the connection the dashboard is on: `Looker`, `Metabase`, `Omni`, `Lightdash`, `Sigma`, `Tableau` or `PowerBI`. It must match the connection's `type` in `listConnections`.

dashboardId.description: The dashboard to add: the `id` of a dashboard from `searchDashboards` on this connection. For Tableau and Sigma, it is a workbook, and for Power BI, a report.

tabId.description: The tab to add: one of the `tabs[].id` values from `getDashboard`, which for Tableau are a workbook's views, for Power BI a report's pages and for Sigma a workbook's pages, or the `tabId` of a Sigma workbook `searchDashboards` found by a link. The datasheet is a picture of that tab, named after it. If omitted, Rollstack adds the tab the dashboard opens on (the first view or page for Tableau, Power BI and Sigma), or, for a dashboard without tabs such as an Omni dashboard, the whole dashboard, named after it. A tab the dashboard doesn't have is rejected.

connectionId.description: The Salesforce connection the report is on: the `id` of a connection from `listConnections`. You must have access to the connection in Rollstack.

connectionType.description: `Salesforce`. It must match the connection's `type` in `listConnections`.

reportId.description: The report to add: the `id` of a `tabular` or `summary` report from `searchDashboards` on this connection. The datasheet contains the report's rows as a table, a summary report's with its groupings as their first columns, and is named after the report. A matrix or joined report is rejected.

connectionId.description: The data warehouse connection the table is on: the `id` of a connection from `listConnections`. You must have your own access to the connection in Rollstack.

connectionType.description: The type of the connection the table is on: `Snowflake` or `Databricks`. It must match the connection's `type` in `listConnections`.

database.description: The database the table is in, as `database` in `searchTables`.

schema.description: The schema the table is in, as `schema` in `searchTables`.

table.description: The table or view to add, as `table` in `searchTables`. The datasheet is named `database.schema.table`, and the slides agent queries it in the warehouse with SQL over all its rows.

connectionId.description: The connection the model is on: the `id` of a connection from `listConnections`. You must have access to the connection in Rollstack, and for Tableau your own Tableau user on it.

connectionType.description: The type of the connection the model is on: `Looker`, `PowerBI` or `Tableau`. It must match the connection's `type` in `listConnections`.

modelId.description: The model to add: the `id` of a Looker explore, Power BI semantic model or Tableau data source from `searchModels` on this connection. The datasheet is named after it and holds no rows: pass its id as `datasheetIds` on `sendReportMessage`, and the slides agent queries the model in its BI tool for the data its slides need. A model the connection doesn't have is rejected.

range.description: The cells to read from the sheet, in A1 notation without the sheet's name, such as `A1:F20`, or `B2` for a single cell. The datasheet contains them as a table and is named after the range. Start the range at the header row so the columns take its names; without a header, they are named `Column 1`, `Column 2` and so on. Hidden rows and columns are left out, and whole columns such as `A:F` aren't accepted.

sheetId.description: The sheet the range is on: one of the `sheets[].id` values from `getSpreadsheet`. A sheet the file doesn't have is rejected.

spreadsheetId.description: The Google Sheets or Excel file to read from: the `id` of a file from `searchSpreadsheets`. It must be a file you added in the app yourself.

idempotencyKey.description: A unique value, such as a UUID, that makes retrying this call safe. A retry with the same key within 24 hours answers the first call's result instead of running it again. Use a new key for each new call. From 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters.

params.description: The ids of what the tool acts on

id.description: The report to act on, by its `id` from `listReports` or `createReport`. Only reports whose `type` is `SlideDeck` work here: another type, such as a Google Slides presentation, returns `400`. You can also copy it from the report's link in Rollstack: it's the part right after `/slides/`.

name: addReportDatasheets
title: Add sources to report
